subject: literature
passage: It was past midnight when the coach set me down at the inn of St. Aurel, and the landlord, a stooped man who carried his candle as though it were heavier than it looked, led me without a word to the only chamber that remained. Above the hearth hung the portrait of a lady in the dress of a former age, whose painted eyes, by some trick of the artist, appeared to follow the light as it moved about the room. <u>I confess I laughed at myself for remarking it, and I took some pains to turn my back upon her while I undressed.</u> Of the night that followed I shall say only this: I did not sleep, and when the gray light came through the shutters, I found that I had, at some hour I cannot recollect, turned the portrait to face the wall.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It establishes that the narrator dismisses the portrait as harmless and is untroubled by it all night.
choices.B: It explains the method by which the artist made the eyes of the portrait appear to move.
choices.C: It exposes a gap between the narrator's professed amusement and his conduct, anticipating his unease.
choices.D: It suggests that the landlord deliberately placed the narrator in a room meant to frighten him.

explanation.why: In the underlined sentence the narrator says he "laughed at" himself for noticing the portrait, yet he also "took some pains" not to face it. That mismatch between words and behavior hints at hidden unease, which the final sentence confirms: he did not sleep and turned the portrait to the wall.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The final sentence shows the narrator sleepless and turning the portrait around, so he was clearly troubled.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The previous sentence mentions "some trick of the artist," but no method is explained anywhere.
explanation.C: Correct. He laughs off the portrait yet avoids facing it, a tension that prepares for his sleepless night.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The landlord gives him "the only chamber that remained," and nothing suggests any intent to frighten him.
